source_text: Tawnr igitur ostensiones cum sint, non oportet adhuc quzerere apud alios yeritatem, quam facile est ab Ecclesia sumere ; cum Apostoli, quasi in depositorium dives, plenissime in eam contulerint omnia que sint veritatis: uti omnis quicunque velit, sumat ex ea potum vitee. Hee est enim vitze introitus; omnes autem reliqui fures sunt et latrones. Propter quod oportet devitare quidem illos; que autem sunt Ecclesiz, cum summa diligentia diligere, et apprehendere veritatis traditionem. Quid enim? Et si de aliqua modica queestione disceptatio esset, nonne oporteret in antiquissimas recurrere ecclesias, in quibus Apostoli conversati sunt, et ab eis de presenti quastione sumere quod certum et re liquidum est? Quid autem si neque Apostoli quidem Scripturas reliquissent nobis, nonne oportebat ordinem sequi_ traditionis, quam tradiderunt iis quibus committebant ecclesias? Cui ordinationi assentiunt multze gentes barbarorum eorum qui in Christum credunt, sine charta vel atramento scriptam habentes per Spiritum in cordibus suis salutem, et veterem traditionem diligenter custodientes, in unum Deum credentes fabricatorem cceli et terree, et omnium quz in eis sunt, per Christum Jesum Dei Filium. Qui propter eminentissimam erga figmentum suum dilectionem, eam que esset ex Virgine generationem sustinuit, ipse per se hominem adunans Deo, et passus sub Pontio Pilato, et resurgens, et in claritate receptus, in gloria venturus Salvator eorum qui salvantur, et judex eorum qui judicantur, et mittens in ignem sternum transfiguratores veritatis, et contemtores Patris sui et adventus ejus. Hane fidem qui sine literis crediderunt, quantum ad sermonem nostrum, barbari sunt: quantum autem ad sententiam, et consuetudinem, et conversationem, propter fidem perquam sapientissimi sunt, et placent Deo, conversantes in omni justitia et castitate et sapientia. Quibus si aliquis annuntiaverit ea que ab hereticis adinventa sunt, proprio sermone eorum colloquens, statim concludentes aures longo longius fugient, ne audire quidem sustinentes blasphemum colloquium. | Sie per illam veterem stolorum traditionem, ne in conceptionem quidem mentis admittunt, quodcunque eorum portentiloquium est, neque enim congregatio fuit apud eos, neque doctrina instituta. 2. Ante Valentinum enim non fuerunt, qui sunt a Valentino; neque ante Marcionem erant, qui sunt a Marcione; neque omnino erant reliqui sensus maligni, quos supra enumeravimus, initiatores et inventores perversitatis eorum fierent. Valentinus enim venit Romam sub Hygino; Pio, et prorogavit tempus usque ad Anicetum. Oerdon autem qui ante Marcionem, et hic sub Hygino, qui fuit octavus episcopus, seepe in ecclesiam veniens, et exhomologesin faciens, sic consummavit, modo quidem latenter docens, modo vero exhomologesin faciens, modo vero ab aliquibus traductus in his que docebat male, et abstentus est a religiosorum hominum conventu. 3. Marcion autem illi succedens invaluit sub Aniceto, !}decimum locum episcopatus continente. Reliqui vero qui vocantur Gnostici, a Menandro Simonis discipulo, quemadmodum ostendimus, accipientes initia, unusquisque eorum, cujus participatus est sententiz, ejus et pater, et antistes apparuit. Omnes autem hi multo posterius, mediantibus jam Ecclesize temporibus, insurrexerunt in suam apostasiam.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, since these are demonstrations, it is not necessary to still seek truth from others, which is easy to take from the Church; since the Apostles, as if into a rich repository, have fully conferred all things of truth into it: so that anyone who wishes may take from it the drink of life. For this is the entrance of life; all the rest, however, are thieves and robbers. On account of which it is necessary to avoid them; but those things which are of the Church, with the greatest diligence to love and to seize the tradition of truth. For what? And if there were a dispute about some small question, would it not be necessary to recur to the most ancient churches, in which the Apostles conversed, and from them to take concerning the present question what is certain and clear? What, however, if the Apostles had not even left us Scriptures, would it not be necessary to follow the order of tradition, which they handed down to those to whom they entrusted the churches? To which ordination many barbarian nations, who believe in Christ, assent, having salvation written in their hearts by the Spirit without chart or ink, and diligently preserving the old tradition, believing in one God, the maker of heaven and earth and all that are in them, through Christ Jesus, the Son of God. Who, on account of his most excellent love towards his creature, sustained the generation which was from the Virgin, himself gathering man to God, and having suffered under Pontius Pilate, and having risen, and having been received in glory, is to come in glory as the Savior of those who are saved, and as the judge of those who are judged, and sending into eternal fire those who transfigure truth, and those who contemptuously regard his Father and his advent. These who have believed without letters, as far as our speech is concerned, are barbarians: but as far as judgment and custom and conversation are concerned, on account of faith they are most wise and pleasing to God, living in all justice and chastity and wisdom. To whom if anyone should announce those things which have been invented by heretics, speaking in their own language, immediately closing their ears they will flee far away, not even enduring to hear the blasphemous conversation. Thus, through that old tradition of the elders, they do not even admit into their conception of mind whatever their portentous speech is, nor was there a gathering among them, nor a doctrine instituted. For before Valentinus, those who are from Valentinus were not; nor before Marcion were those who are from Marcion; nor were there at all the remaining malignant senses, which we enumerated above, to become the initiators and inventors of their perversity. For Valentinus came to Rome under Hyginus; and Pius; and prolonged his time until Anicetus. But Cerdo, who was before Marcion, and this under Hyginus, who was the eighth bishop, coming often into the church and making confession, thus consummated, sometimes teaching secretly, sometimes making confession, sometimes being handed over by some to those things which he taught badly, and was absent from the gathering of religious men. And Marcion, succeeding him, grew strong under Anicetus, holding the tenth place of the episcopate. The rest, however, who are called Gnostics, taking their beginnings from Menander, the disciple of Simon, as we have shown, each one of them, whose sentiment he has participated in, has appeared as his father and bishop. All these, however, much later, with the times of the Church intervening, rose up into their own apostasy.
pass_b_english: Therefore, since these demonstrations exist, there is no need to seek the truth from others any longer, for it is easy to receive it from the Church. The Apostles, like men depositing a treasure in a rich repository, have fully entrusted to her all things that belong to the truth, so that everyone who wishes may draw from her the drink of life. For this is the entrance to life; all the others, however, are thieves and robbers. On this account we must avoid them, but we must love and cling to the things that belong to the Church with the greatest diligence, laying hold of the tradition of the truth.

For consider: if a dispute arose over some minor question, would it not be necessary to turn to the most ancient churches, those in which the Apostles themselves dwelt, and to learn from them what is certain and clear regarding the present issue? What is more, if the Apostles had not even left us the Scriptures, would it not have been necessary to follow the order of tradition which they handed down to those to whom they entrusted the churches?

To this order many nations of barbarians assent, those who believe in Christ. They have salvation written in their hearts by the Spirit, without paper or ink, and they diligently preserve the ancient tradition. They believe in one God, the Maker of heaven and earth and all things in them, through Christ Jesus, the Son of God. Because of his surpassing love for his creation, he endured the birth from the Virgin, himself uniting man to God. He suffered under Pontius Pilate, rose again, was received in glory, and will come in glory as the Savior of those who are saved and the Judge of those who are judged. He will send into eternal fire those who distort the truth, and those who despise his Father and his coming.

These men, who have believed without written documents, are barbarians as far as our language is concerned; but as far as judgment, custom, and conduct go, they are most wise through faith and pleasing to God, living in all justice, chastity, and wisdom. If anyone should announce to them the inventions of the heretics, speaking in their own tongue, they will immediately stop their ears and flee far away, refusing even to endure such blasphemous talk. Thus, through that ancient tradition of the elders, they do not admit even into the conception of their minds whatever portentous speech the heretics utter. For there was no assembly among them, nor any instituted doctrine.

For before Valentinus came, those who are from Valentinus did not exist; nor before Marcion did those from Marcion exist; nor were there at all the remaining malignant opinions which we enumerated above to become the authors and inventors of their perversity. Valentinus came to Rome under Hyginus; he flourished under Pius, and remained until Anicetus. Cerdo, who preceded Marcion, also lived under Hyginus, the eighth bishop. He came often into the church and made confession, but he ended in this way: sometimes he taught secretly, sometimes he made confession, sometimes he was rebuked by some for the evil things he taught, and he kept away from the assembly of the godly. Marcion, succeeding him, grew strong under Anicetus, who held the tenth place in the episcopate. The rest, who are called Gnostics, received their beginnings from Menander, the disciple of Simon, as we have shown. Each one of them, whose opinion he adopted, became the father and bishop of his own sect. All these men rose up in their apostasy much later, during the intervening times of the Church.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version that maintains the semantic integrity of the original. All clauses, including the complex descriptions of the Christological tenets and the historical succession of heretical leaders, are preserved. The distinction between 'barbarians' in speech versus 'wise' in faith is correctly maintained.
